Subject: MAP: compliance touchpoint — ownership & next steps (data handling)

Hi Emily — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and an attached MAP draft (see MAP-draft-Medlytics-v1.xlsx) focused on the Data Handling & Compliance milestone we discussed.

Summary of the call:
- Scope: inference for radiology-report summarization (PHI in input).
- Core asks: retention policy for request/response logs, audit trail requirements, whether logs may contain PHI, and procurement/BAA expectations.

Proposed MAP milestone (Data handling & compliance) — draft items:
1) Retention policy for request/response logs (audit): propose "7 years" for audit logs, shorter retention for non-audit telemetry (30 days).
2) Audit trail: immutable access logs with user id, timestamp, action.
3) PHI handling: option to enable in-flight redaction and strict access controls; prefer Private deployment or Dedicated with customer encryption keys for PHI workloads.
4) Evidence: SOC 2 + encryption attestation + sample audit logs.

Asks / next steps:
- Can you confirm Medlytics target close date for this MAP milestone? (we suggested 2026-10-20 as a placeholder)
- Please confirm procurement contact for BAA and legal review (CC'd procurement if useful).
- Emily: please flag any non-negotiable retention windows or specific regulatory obligations (state law, HIPAA clauses) we should model.
- Internal: Lauren/Monica/Sooj — can you review the attached and confirm owners for retention, logging, and evidence collection?

Attachment: MAP-draft-Medlytics-v1.xlsx (MAP table + milestone rows).

Thanks — Jordan

Thanks Jordan — appreciate the clear recap. A couple quick items from our side: 

1) Procurement contact: procurement@medlytics.com (I've looped them in). They will handle BAA negotiation and the redlines for standard Data Processing Agreement.
2) PHI: yes, our radiology inputs are PHI. Critical constraints:
   - Logs must not retain unredacted PHI fields in plaintext by default.
   - We will require an ability to scope logs so that full request/response bodies with PHI are only retained for a limited, auditable set of accounts and under explicit retention policies.
3) Target date: Can we aim for milestone close by 2026-10-15? That aligns with our internal compliance review window.

Questions:
- Does Redwood offer an automated redaction option or a recommended pattern for minimizing PHI in logs?
- For Dedicated/Private options: what is your recommended path if we need customer-managed keys?

I'll review the attached MAP and circle back with procurement on the BAA timeline.

—Emily

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: compliance touchpoint — ownership & next steps (data handling)

Thanks for the notes — adding technical constraints and proposed owners for the MAP draft. High level answers to Emily's questions first:

- Automated redaction: Redwood has a configurable pre-ingest redaction pipeline (pattern-based + ML PII detectors). For PHI workloads we recommend enabling rule-based scrubbing on PII fields and configuring a redaction policy prior to persisting logs. That is available today as an opt-in policy on Hosted, and is standard on Private.
- Customer-managed keys: Supported in Private deployment (KMS/HSM integration) and available as an option for Dedicated via our managed KMS integration. We should note this dependency in the MAP.

Technical proposals for the MAP milestone (please add to the draft):
- Retention windows:
  • Audit logs (immutable): 7 years (owner: Soojin Lee)
  • Full request/response (with PHI): default 30 days; can be extended per account with explicit documented approval (owner: Monica Patel for procurement ops)
  • Redacted copies: 1 year
- Audit trail requirements:
  • Immutable append-only audit store with SHA-256 hashes, access records, and exportable CSV for audits.
  • Separate access logs for admin actions and data access.
- Encryption & KMS:
  • Encryption at rest & in transit mandatory.
  • Customer-managed keys recommended for PHI workloads (Private preferred).
- Evidence & dependencies:
  • Provide latest SOC 2 Type II report, encryption attestation, and sample redacted audit logs (owner: Soojin Lee).
  • Dependency: procurement/legal must complete BAA + DPA (owner: Monica Patel to coordinate with Medlytics procurement).
  • Dependency: architecture review for Private deployment if customer opts for on-premises HSM (owner: Lauren Bishop to coordinate infra sizing).

I'll attach a stripped-down controls matrix to the MAP (controls-matrix-template.csv) for Emily's team to annotate required controls.

Notes on risk/acceptance:
- If Medlytics requires indefinite retention of full request/response bodies with PHI, that will push us toward Private or a never-retain-for-hosted policy; we should flag that as a potential timeline blocker.

Soojin
Soojin Lee

Subject: Re: MAP: compliance touchpoint — ownership & next steps (data handling)

Emily — thanks, that helps. Quick MAP-update and proposed owners/target dates below. I updated the attached draft and included the controls matrix.

Consolidated MAP milestone: Data handling & compliance (final draft items)
- Retention: Audit logs 7 years (Owner: Soojin Lee)
- Full request/response (PHI): default 30 days; extension only via documented approval (Owner: Monica Patel / Medlytics procurement)
- Redacted copies: 1 year (Owner: Soojin Lee)
- Audit trail: immutable, exportable; include admin access logs (Owner: Soojin Lee)
- Encryption & KMS: encryption in transit/rest; customer-managed keys option (Owner: Lauren Bishop)
- Evidence: SOC 2 + sample redacted logs (Owner: Soojin Lee)

Dependencies & blockers:
- BAA/DPA execution (Owner: Monica Patel) — required before retention exceptions are approved.
- Architecture review for Private (Owner: Lauren Bishop) — if Medlytics chooses Private for key isolation, add ~3 weeks to timeline.

Target close date: 2026-10-20 (requested) — Emily had proposed 2026-10-15; let's aim for 10/20 to allow procurement + SOC evidence packaging. If Medlytics can expedite procurement we can compress to 10/15.

Next steps (action items):
- Monica: kick off BAA with procurement@medlytics.com and share expected timeline (by 2026-09-21).
- Soojin: prepare SOC 2 extracts and a redacted sample audit log (by 2026-09-24).
- Lauren: start Private sizing thread if needed and provide estimate for architecture review duration (by 2026-09-22).
- Emily: confirm if Medlytics can accept the default 30-day full-body retention for Hosted or if an extension request will be submitted.

Emily — please reply-all with your preferred target and whether procurement has a hard SLA for BAA review so we can tighten the date.

Thanks — Jordan
